The formatted string of one block, for the manuscript

Source: R/formatters.R
txt.Rd

txt() returns one string of the formatted value of a block, from the real blocks.qs2 of the version. A manuscript calls it inline, for example `r pbn::txt("Results para 1: effect", version = "v02")`.

Usage

txt(name, row = 1, col = NULL, version = NULL, home = NULL)

Arguments

name

The name of the block in blocks, one string.

row

The row of the formatted value, a whole number from 1.

col

The column of the formatted value when the formatter returns a data.frame: a name or a number. NULL is right only for a character vector or a data.frame with one column.

version

The version, for example "v01". The default NULL is the version of the last initialize_project() in this R session.

home

The project folder. The default NULL is the folder of the last initialize_project() in this R session.

Value

One string.

Details

txt() reads the raw value as read_blocks() does: <home>/<version>_results/real/blocks.qs2 when it exists, which save_results(), update_blocks() and import_blocks() write. In a one-file project without that file, it reads fake/ with a warning, see the section The folder fake/ of initialize_project(). It formats the value at each call, so a change of a formatter needs no new blocks.qs2.

After initialize_project() of version and home in this R session, txt() takes the block from that session. Else it reads <version>_functions/blocks.R without running it. It then needs a call pbn::block() with a string format for the block name, and it evaluates only the function assignments of <version>_functions/formatters.R. Their parent environment holds the top-level assignments of the other .R files of the functions folder, such as CFG, in the order that initialize_project() sources them. A top-level call that is not an assignment, such as cat(), does not run. The default home is then the working folder. The default version needs initialize_project().

txt() stops when the block, the row, the column or blocks.qs2 is missing. It also stops when the block is not a pbn::block(), or when the cell is not a string. It stops on a raw value that breaks the rule of block().

See also

block(), show_block().
